transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I just keep getting stuck on this... this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek. 

I notice it all the time in photos, and especially under the bright lights at the store where I work. Even when other people tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, it just feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me. So, yeah, it's just been bothering me a lot and I wanted to talk to someone about it.
Do you believe for certain that the spot on your face is noticeable to other people?

Um, I guess I'm not totally sure. Like, I don't know for absolute certain. Because, you know, my friends and family tell me they don't even see it, so... part of me thinks maybe it isn't as obvious as I think it is. But then when I'm actually standing there at the register, it just really feels like people are staring right at it. So I guess I kind of go back and forth on it.
Because of that spot, do you find yourself checking or touching it over and over?

Yeah, I do. Um, when I'm on my breaks at work, I usually end up just checking my face in the bathroom mirror. I'll spend time trying to fix my hair around it to see if I can hide it better. And I also catch myself comparing myself to the girls who come through my checkout line. It actually gets kind of frustrating because sometimes I take so long checking in the mirror that I end up being late getting back to the register.
Have you started avoiding social situations because you feel embarrassed about that spot on your face?

Um, no, not really. I mean, it definitely bothers me, but I still go out and do things. I still hang out with my friends and go to work. I might feel a little self-conscious while I'm out, but I haven't stopped going places or anything like that.
How much is this concern about the spot interfering with your life?

Well, it's mostly affecting my work, I think. Like I said, I take too long in the bathroom checking the mirror, and... well, my manager has definitely noticed that I've been coming back late from my breaks. And I guess I've been moving a bit slower at the register, too, because I get so distracted feeling like people are looking at me. It really worries me because I'm trying to get a promotion right now, and I just feel like this is making me look super unreliable to my boss.
Aside from this spot on your face, is there any other main reason you feel people are judging you?
Um, no, not really. It's honestly just the spot. I mean, I don't think there's anything else people would be judging me for... it's really just that one thing that bothers me.
On a typical day, how much time do you spend thinking about that spot on your face?

Um, I'm not really sure exactly. I haven't timed it or anything like that. It just kind of... pops into my head throughout the day. Like I said, I think about it a lot when I'm at work or if I have to talk to customers at the register, but I couldn't give you an exact amount of hours or anything. It's just on my mind a lot.
Would you say you spend at least an hour a day thinking about that spot on your face?

Yeah, definitely at least an hour. I mean, that's really why I decided to come in to see someone. I just keep getting stuck on this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek. I see it all the time in photos, and it looks really bad under the bright store lights at work. Even when other people tell me they don't really see it, I just... I can't shake it. It feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me. So yeah, thinking about all that definitely adds up to at least an hour a day.
Do you also have other repetitive unwanted thoughts or rituals that are not about your appearance?

No, I don't think so. It's really just my face. I don't get stuck on any other thoughts, and I don't have any, like, routines or habits I feel like I have to do. It's just that one spot that bothers me.
How distressed does thinking about that spot make you feel?

Um, it definitely bothers me. I wouldn't say I'm, like, having a breakdown over it or anything, but it makes me feel pretty frustrated and self-conscious. When I'm at the register and I feel like people are staring at it, I just get really embarrassed and kind of down about myself. It's just... annoying that it upsets me and I can't just let it go.
If the spot on your face were not there, would you still feel very nervous that people were judging you?

Um, no, I don't think so. I'm usually pretty fine talking to people. If my skin was just even and that spot was gone, I think I'd feel totally normal ringing up customers. I don't really worry about people judging me for anything else, it's just... just that one thing on my face.
Have you been feeling depressed or down most of the day nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I get bummed out about my face sometimes, like I said, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed all day. Most of the time I'm okay, just going to work and doing my normal stuff. It's just when I start thinking about the spot that I get a little down.
When other people look closely at that spot on your face, do they usually say they can see it, or do they say they really can’t notice anything wrong?

Um, they usually say they don't really see it. Like, they'll look and say they can't notice anything wrong at all. But... I don't know, I just keep getting stuck on it. It's this tiny uneven spot right around my nose and cheek, and especially under those bright store lights at work, or if I see a photo of myself, it just looks so obvious to me. So even when my friends or family tell me they don't see it, it still feels like it's the very first thing the customers and my managers notice when they look at me.
